name: gold_for_the_portal

caption: why does grandma feed the nether portal 😶
logline: Every night Grandma throws one gold ingot into the Nether portal in the cellar and every morning a gift comes back, so her grandson Nico is sure Grandpa is alive over there, until he throws in a whole stack to buy Grandpa's way home and a piglin steps out wearing Grandpa's helmet.
question: why tf does grandma throw gold into a nether portal every night?
premise: Grandpa went into the Nether 25 years ago wearing Grandma's gold helmet with the blue stripe ('gold keeps you safe in the Nether') and never came back. Every night since, Grandma throws one gold ingot into the portal in the cellar (9,000 of them), and every morning something comes back out of it: obsidian, string, ender pearls, fire resistance potions. Grandma says he's still trading. Her grandson keeps the gifts in a barrel and knows Grandpa is alive.
twist: The gifts are a piglin's barters: piglins take a gold ingot and throw back a random item from the barter list. Grandpa died over there long ago; a piglin picked his helmet up where he fell (piglins pick up and wear gold armour) and has traded with Grandma every night since, because she is the only one who feeds it gold. Grandma has known for years ('Just one, sweetie. One's plenty.'). Tonight Nico throws in a whole stack to buy Grandpa's way home, the piglin comes through after the gold, and it is wearing Grandpa's helmet. Shaking (a piglin in the Overworld starts to zombify), it turns after the one more ingot Grandma tosses into the purple: she sends it home.

lines.text: My grandma has thrown / NINE THOUSAND / gold ingots / into a PORTAL.

lines.say: My grandma has thrown nine thousand gold ingots into a portal.
lines.retake: owner 2026-11-10: a pause (it sounds like a breath) before NINE THOUSAND. Re-take as one continuous phrase, no breath or pause before the number (the continuous-take gate). The emphasis comes from the voice, not a stop.

lines.text: One every NIGHT. / And every MORNING, / something comes BACK.

lines.retake: check at the re-take (lead, 2026-11-10): forced alignment puts voicing 0.22-0.40 s before the vowel of 'One': listen for a breath or hum before the line; re-take if heard.

lines.text: OBSIDIAN. / STRING. / ENDER PEARLS. / A potion that makes you FIREPROOF.

lines.text: Twenty-five years ago, / Grandma gave Grandpa / her gold HELMET. / With a BLUE stripe.

lines.text: Gold keeps you SAFE / in the NETHER, she said. / He went IN. / He never came BACK.

lines.note: quoting her proudly, then the energy drops for the last sentence; a short stop before it

lines.text: I keep his gifts / in a BARREL. / Grandma says / he's still TRADING.
lines.note: bright again, sure of it; the last word said like a fact everybody knows

lines.text: So he's ALIVE. / I KNOW it.
lines.note: full volume, certain, a little defiant, like someone said he wasn't

lines.direction: gentle and firm, a small smile; a beat after the name
lines.say: Just one, sweetie. <short pause> One's plenty.
lines.owner_note: 2026-11-10 'Who is nico?': the narrator's name is never set up, so Grandma doesn't say it. Re-voice L08.

lines.text: When she went to BED, / I threw in / ALL my gold. / SIXTY-FOUR. / To buy his way HOME.
lines.note: sneaky and fast, then huge hope on the last words

lines.text: Then I sat / and WAITED. / And something / stepped OUT.
lines.say: Then I sat and waited. <short pause> And something stepped out.
lines.note: slower, full volume, real nerves creeping in; a held beat before the last two words
